sections.heading: The setup
sections.body: The S&P 500 sits mid-range for the past month at 7,637.76, about 44% of the way up its 30-day band between 7,551.81 and 7,747.71. The Nasdaq 100 trades closer to its monthly highs at roughly 72% of range, while the Euro Stoxx 50 sits lower in its own band at 29%. The VIX at 15.44 is in the lower third of its 1-month range (32%), consistent with a calm volatility backdrop heading into the week. This week's earnings load is light — 6 reports across four sectors, with consumer names (AutoZone, Costco, General Mills, Thor Industries) accounting for 4 of the 6.

sections.heading: What to watch
sections.body: Tue: AZO US and THO US both report into the consumer-cyclical group, where the sector's median 3-day reaction sits flat at -0.15% across 497 tickers. Wed: CTAS US reports into industrials, this week's weakest sector at -1.43% median across 604 names, while GIS US reports the same day into consumer-defensive (-0.51% median, 362 names). Thu: COST US reports into that same consumer-defensive group, and SNX US reports into technology — the only sector on this week's slate with a positive median reaction, +0.87% across 567 tickers.

sections.heading: Signals to trust
sections.body: None of this week's reporters sit in a sector with a strong recent reaction. The sector table is led by mining (+6.62% median across 172 tickers, with an unusually thick 2,630-item news window), alternative-asset-management (+2.93% median, 6 tickers, 232 news items), and copper (+2.63% median, 6 tickers, 248 news items) — none of which have names reporting this week, so this week's actual earnings carry more modest sector momentum than the broader tape.
